topic: Objective Mismatch & Fluke Bias in Spark ALS Top-N Generalization
problem_statement: Explain why complex Spark Matrix Factorization (ALS) underperforms simple Popularity Count on both Validation (0 vs 6,059 hits) and Test (1 vs 5,958 hits) splits.
root_cause: Objective function mismatch: Spark MLlib explicit ALS minimizes squared rating error (RMSE) on observed interactions rather than pairwise ranking loss. On highly sparse (99.75%) long-tail datasets, rare items with 1-2 five-star ratings easily attain unbounded high dot products (5.0-10.0), dominating >95% of Top-20 recommendation slots (Fluke Bias). Popularity Count directly models marginal item interaction probability P(Item), matching real-world blockbuster consumption propensities.
solution_or_decision: Document this finding as an essential empirical baseline in the MoodGraph thesis. Explicit rating regression without popularity shrinkage cannot serve as a reliable standalone Top-N recommender, providing clear motivation for Task 3B (Knowledge Graph Semantic Path Exploration) and Task 3C (Hybrid Recommendation Architecture).
evidence: Validation: Count HR@10=0.05519 vs ALS HR@10=0.00000. Test: Count HR@10=0.05357 vs ALS HR@10=0.00001. Fluke 1-rating items occupy >95% slots in ALS recommendations.
